pack.title: Tipping & checkout pressure
pack.description: The tipped tablet turn. Tip for service, not for being watched.

scenarios.setting: Counter pickup. The cashier flips the tablet: 25%, 30%, 35%.
scenarios.jab: It's just going to ask you a quick question.

replies.line: No tip on counter pickup. Thanks.
replies.why: It states your policy as a fact about the situation, not a judgment of him.
replies.delivery: Warm tone, final words. Then tap zero without lingering.

replies.why: It answers the tablet's question out loud so there's nothing awkward left unsaid.

replies.line: I'll pass on this one — appreciate you though.
replies.why: Thanks plus a clear no keeps the human moment intact while your wallet stays shut.

replies.line: The tablet and I disagree on what happened here.
replies.why: Blaming the tablet lets you both laugh while you tap zero together.

trap.line: This tipping stuff is out of control, honestly.
trap.why: Lecturing the cashier punishes the person with the least power over the policy.

scenarios.setting: Restaurant. The server hovers while you split the bill with friends.
scenarios.jab: Just so you know, the machine adds eighteen percent automatically.

replies.line: Then we're settled. Thank you for the evening.
replies.why: It treats the auto-gratuity as the end of the transaction, which it is.
It closes the check the way the policy already did, with no encore.

replies.line: Perfect, that makes it easy — thanks for looking after us.
replies.why: Gratitude for the service lands better than extra money ever could.
